clue.text: American politician introduced to a baby

indicators.note: something introduced to another thing is put inside it, so the first pair goes within the last word

parts.note: 'a' as in 'five pounds a day', i.e. per
A is a standard abbreviation for American
Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A US politician being presented to an infant, as at a photo opportunity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A' does double duty in the surface as an article, but cryptically it means 'per', as in a price per item. 'Baby' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To baby someone is to indulge and coddle them, the verb sense matching pamper exactly.

clue.text: Make a mistake, going topless in church recess

indicators.note: losing the top means the first letter of the word, written downwards, is dropped

parts.note: to lapse is to slip up

explanation.surface: Someone blunders by going topless inside a church alcove.
explanation.definitionFit: An apse is the semicircular recess at the east end of a church, usually housing the altar.

clue.text: Coated area of meat packaging isn't wide

indicators.note: packaging wraps round its contents, so the meat surrounds what follows

parts.note: a kind of meat
colloquial form of isn't
W is the cricket abbreviation for a wide

explanation.surface: A butcher's note about a wrapped joint of meat that is narrow rather than broad.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a wide is a ball bowled out of the batter's reach, scored as W.
explanation.definitionFit: Paintwork is the painted surface of something, an area covered in coats of paint.

clue.text: Ex-President is concerning once more, I conceded

indicators.note: conceding means giving something up, so the letter I is surrendered from the word before it

parts.note: re means about or concerning
a synonym

explanation.surface: A former president admits, once again, that he gave way on something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I conceded' reads as a confession, but it tells you to give up the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan served as US President from 1981 to 1989, so he is a former holder of the office.

clue.text: Salad ingredient is copper brown when bit of celery added

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

indicators.note: a bit of a word is a single letter of it, here its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of celery
umber is a brown earth pigment

explanation.surface: A recipe note: a salad turns coppery brown once some celery is mixed in.
explanation.walkthrough: The celery letter is added between the copper and the brown.
explanation.definitionFit: Cucumber is the long green vegetable sliced into salads, a typical ingredient of one.

clue.text: Hail Newcastle as 'surprisingly spotless'

indicators.note: surprisingly suggests the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone praises the city of Newcastle as unexpectedly tidy.
explanation.definitionFit: Clean as a whistle is an idiom meaning perfectly clean, with no stain or fault.

clue.text: Cocaine gets in the way of celebratory drink

parts.note: C is slang for cocaine
hampers means obstructs

explanation.surface: Drugs spoil a party where bubbly is being drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: Champers is British slang for champagne.
explanation.definitionFit: Champagne is the classic wine for toasting a success or celebration.

clue.text: Quality setter runs with it

parts.note: the setter refers to themself as me
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
taken as written; with joins it on

explanation.surface: A dog-show judge praising a top-quality red setter that is running.
explanation.definitionFit: Merit is worth or excellence, the good quality something possesses.

clue.text: Curses temp leaving Miles with vile sex deviant

indicators.note: deviant means departing from the norm, so the letters stray from their order
the abbreviation for miles departs, so that letter is taken away from the word before

parts.note: taken as written
M is the abbreviation for miles
taken as written

explanation.surface: An office worker storming out after an encounter with a lewd pervert, cursing.
explanation.walkthrough: TEMP without M leaves TEP, which joins VILE SEX to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Expletives are swear words, the oaths someone utters when cursing.

clue.text: When quietly furious, breathe audibly

parts.note: as can mean when
p for piano, the musical direction for soft
a synonym

explanation.surface: Someone who is silently enraged breathes heavily.
explanation.definitionFit: To aspirate is to pronounce a sound with an audible breath, as with an initial h.

clue.text: Sudden belch after heart transplant in outskirts of Ashgabat

indicators.note: in places the altered word inside the outer letters
outskirts are the edges, so only the first and last letters count

parts.note: first and last letters of the Turkmen capital

indicators.note: transplanting the heart means the central pair of letters is swapped round

parts.note: a synonym

explanation.surface: A patient in the capital of Turkmenistan burps unexpectedly after cardiac surgery.
explanation.walkthrough: The heart transplant swaps the two middle letters of the belch; Ashgabat is the capital of Turkmenistan.
explanation.definitionFit: Abrupt describes something happening suddenly and without warning.

clue.text: Perhaps Del Boy tours Spain cycling in anorak?

indicators.note: to tour a place is to go all round it, so the surname surrounds the country
cycling moves letters round from front to back, like a wheel turning

parts.note: taken as written
Del Boy is Derek Trotter of the TV sitcom Only Fools and Horses; perhaps marks him as one example

explanation.surface: A TV wide boy travelling round Spain by bike, wearing a hooded jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: SPAIN cycled two places becomes AINSP. An anorak, beyond the jacket, is British slang for an obsessive enthusiast, and the trainspotter is the stereotype.
explanation.definitionFit: A trainspotter collects locomotive numbers and is the archetypal example of a nerdy hobbyist.

clue.text: Cook put a meal in to cook

indicators.note: cooking mixes ingredients up, so the letters get stirred into a new order

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A kitchen instruction to put a meal in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Cook appears twice: first as the definition, in the sense of cooking the books.
explanation.definitionFit: To cook figures is to falsify them, which is to manipulate them dishonestly.

clue.text: Government official briefly in Irish county

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: head of a town or city government

explanation.surface: A civic official making a short visit to Ireland.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayo is a county on the west coast of Ireland, in the province of Connacht.

clue.text: Get rid of drug at home; just make it?

parts.note: a synonym
E is slang for ecstasy
in means at home

explanation.surface: Someone flushes their drugs at home, hoping to get away with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To scrape in is to succeed by the narrowest margin, as when barely passing an exam.

clue.text: Various newspapers covering frozen water on lake is invaluable

indicators.note: covering means wrapping round, so the newspapers enclose what follows

parts.note: the press is newspapers collectively
a definition
L for lake; on means it comes after the ice

explanation.surface: Newspaper reports on a frozen lake are said to be of huge value.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On' in a down clue puts the lake letter after the frozen water.
explanation.definitionFit: Invaluable means too valuable to measure, just as priceless means beyond any price.

clue.text: One case of Penny doing headstand in 6 rooms

indicators.note: a letter standing on its head is turned upside down and becomes a different letter in the same spot

parts.note: the answer to 6 down
penny is abbreviated p, written in lower case

explanation.surface: A cryptic picture of a coin flipping over inside some rooms.
explanation.walkthrough: One case means one letter-case: lower-case p turned upside down looks like b, so the P in the answer to 6 becomes B.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambers are rooms, especially private or official ones such as a judge's or barrister's.

clue.text: Was hard to be upset after Little Richard towed vehicle

parts.note: a short form of Richard

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disordered, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: was plus H, the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: It was tough to be upset once the singer Little Richard had been towed away.
explanation.walkthrough: Little Richard looks like the rock and roll singer, but here it means a shortened Richard.
explanation.definitionFit: A rickshaw is a light two-wheeled cart pulled along by a person on foot.

clue.text: I live with ten horny climbers

definitions.note: plural, but ibex is its own plural

parts.note: taken as written
to be is to exist or live
X is the Roman numeral ten; with joins it on

explanation.surface: A boast about sharing a home with ten lusty mountaineers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ibex are wild mountain goats with big curved horns, famous for scaling sheer rock faces.

clue.text: Big names catching international flight

indicators.note: catching means seizing and holding, so the big names enclose the abbreviation

parts.note: celebrities
I is an abbreviation for international

explanation.surface: Celebrities boarding an overseas plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flight' suggests air travel, but here it is a flight of steps.
explanation.definitionFit: A flight is a series of steps between floors, which is a set of stairs.

clue.text: Very select group must become excited about IT

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the rearranged letters go round the computing term
excited means stirred up, so the letters are agitated into a new order

parts.note: ten letters to rearrange
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demand that an exclusive club get enthusiastic about information technology.
explanation.walkthrough: 'IT' looks like information technology, but here its two letters are simply wrapped by the rearranged ones.
explanation.definitionFit: A subcommittee is a small group drawn from a larger committee, so its membership is narrowly chosen.

clue.text: Firm support for crisis response team

parts.note: Co. is the abbreviation for company
a bra supports the bust

explanation.surface: Strong backing for an emergency task force.
explanation.walkthrough: COBRA, named after Cabinet Office Briefing Room A, is the British government committee convened during national emergencies.
explanation.definitionFit: COBRA meetings bring ministers and officials together to coordinate the UK's handling of a crisis.

clue.text: Nude, rudely push German away

indicators.note: sending something away removes it, so the German abbreviation is taken out

parts.note: to barge is to shove rudely
G is the abbreviation for German

explanation.surface: A naked man shoves a German aside.
explanation.definitionFit: Bare means unclothed, the same as nude.

clue.text: Rock icon from Jamaica cut bass jams

indicators.note: to jam something is to squeeze it in, so the trimmed name holds the bass abbreviation
cut means shortened, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Bob Marley, the Jamaican reggae star
B is the abbreviation for bass in music

explanation.surface: A Jamaican rock star trims his bass-heavy jam sessions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rock icon' reads as one phrase, but Rock is the definition and the icon is Marley.
explanation.definitionFit: Marble is a metamorphic rock formed from limestone, prized by sculptors and builders.

clue.text: Pureed pulses alongside cooked stomachs of animals with three feet

parts.note: tripe is the cooked stomach lining of cattle or sheep
dal is an Indian dish of puréed lentils

explanation.surface: A menu describing dal served beside tripe.
explanation.walkthrough: Alongside lets the dal come after the tripe though it is named first.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripedal means having or using three feet, as an adjective describing such creatures.

clue.text: Small rescue dog bites backside of Japanese emperor

indicators.note: biting holds something between the teeth, so the dog's letters close round that letter

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
Lassie is the collie of film and TV who rescues people

indicators.note: the backside is the rear, so only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: last letter of Japanese

explanation.surface: A little rescue mutt nips the rear of a Japanese emperor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese emperor' reads as one phrase, but only emperor is the definition. The small Lassie takes E in its jaws right after the S.
explanation.definitionFit: Haile Selassie was Emperor of Ethiopia from 1930 to 1974.

clue.text: Embassy's temporarily restricting plan of action

indicators.note: restricting means confining, so the letters are held within the words around them

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: An embassy is for now limiting its strategy.
explanation.definitionFit: A system is a method or organised scheme for doing something, like a plan of action.
